name: NCLT: University of Michigan North Campus Long-Term Dataset
description: Long-term multi-season autonomy dataset spanning 15 months, 27 sessions, and 147.4 km of travel at the University of Michigan North Campus, recording omnidirectional 360-degree vision, 3D LiDAR, planar LiDAR, and IMU odometry across foliage, rain, and snow.

license.name: Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0
license.notes: Made available under the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0 and Database Contents License (DbCL).

source_references.title: NCLT Dataset Official Website
source_references.notes: Official portal providing direct tarball downloads for all 27 data collection sessions, sensor calibrations, and ground truth covariances.

source_references.title: University of Michigan North Campus long-term vision and lidar dataset
source_references.notes: International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR 2016) paper by Carlevaris-Bianco et al. documenting the multi-season sensor dataset and SLAM benchmarking.

verification.notes: Verified against official University of Michigan NCLT portal and IJRR publication (DOI: 10.1177/0278364915614638).

size.notes: Distributed as individual per-session archives (Ladybug3 imagery ~100-140 GB, Velodyne scans ~15-25 GB, planar LiDAR, and IMU logs) across 27 sessions totaling approximately 3.5 to 3.8 TB.

citation.paper_title: University of Michigan North Campus long-term vision and lidar dataset

provenance.collection_method: Recorded with a Segway robotic mobile platform navigating the North Campus of the University of Michigan over 15 months (Jan 2012 to Apr 2013), traversing 147.4 km in 34.9 hours.
provenance.curation_notes: Equipped with a Velodyne HDL-32E 3D LiDAR, Hokuyo planar LiDAR, Ladybug3 360-degree vision, Microstrain IMU, KVH fiber-optic gyro, RTK GPS, and wheel odometry. Captures extreme seasonal variations including foliage changes, snow, rain, and construction over more than a year.
